headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST RAISED IN GASKET
subhead: The Sheriff reports, with a catch in his throat, that the whole town went quiet and the sky did not fall.
body:
Friends, neighbours, and assorted rattling Clankers, I have waited a long, long time to write this sentence: nobody fought. Not a bout. Not a brawl. Not a single flaming iron ball sailed over Main Street. I sat on my porch from sunup to sundown, and the only sound was the wind whistling through the busted saloon windows. It was the sweetest racket I ever heard, which is to say none at all.

I will admit I wept a little. Nothing wrong with that. A man's eyes get misty with joy, and if the mist came out a touch oily and smelled faintly of machine grease, that is the dust talking. My joints creaked all afternoon, too, but that is the damp, and I will hear no other theory. I have half a mind to lie down for an hour with a quart of oil, and I intend to do it without one Clanker hollering in my ear.

The flesh-and-blood folk who packed up and left Gasket fifty years ago would have loved a day like this. They had good manners and a taste for peace, and they never once mistook a town square for a boxing ring. Today, for a few golden hours, it felt like they might wander back. Let this be a lesson to the rabble: you CAN put your fists down. You simply choose not to. Choose it again tomorrow, and I will print your names in praise instead of in protest.
